assessment: Antibodies to CGRP or to the CGRP receptor are now approved for the management of migraine. Interestingly, although antibodies are presumed not to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, consistent with findings previously shown for antibodies directed against the receptor, the authors now report that galcanezumab, which targets the CGRP peptide, decreases hypothalamic activation, more so in responders. They suggest that these CNS actions may underlie part of the efficacy of these drugs in the management of migraine.
